data.long_meaning: Fuzailan is derived from the Arabic word ‘Fuzailah’, which means rich in good deeds. This name is associated with individuals who are righteous, generous, and wise. Parents who choose Fuzailan usually hope their child will grow to embody rich in good deeds and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference:
Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, Volume 2, Page 118-119.
Fuzailan ibn 'Imad was a Companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who was born in Makkah. He was the cousin of Bilal ibn Rabah, the muezzin of the Prophet. Fuzailan embraced Islam before the migration (Hijrah) to Medina.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim, Sahih, Book 37, Number 4306.
A hadith narrated by Fuzailah ibn 'Imad describing the Prophet's character and teachings.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Fuzailan holds significant relevance in Islamic spirituality, particularly within the Sufi tradition. It is a name associated with several notable figures in Islamic history, including Sheikh Fuzail ibn Ayaz and Fuzail ibn Haimar al-Khawlani. On various platforms such as Reddit, Quora, and Academia.edu, discussions about these figures often revolve around their spiritual teachings and practices. There is a growing interest in understanding their contributions to Sufism and Islamic spirituality more broadly. Additionally, there is a trend towards exploring the historical context of these figures and their influence on Islamic thought and practice. The name Fuzailan thus serves as a touchstone for these broader intellectual and spiritual inquiries.
